title: Can two threads collide?
prompt: An offset is a sum of digits: (coefficient, largest value) pairs, one per index. Write unique(digits): true when, sorted by coefficient from largest to smallest, every coefficient is greater than the most the smaller digits can add up to (the sum of coefficient · largest value over them). A digit whose largest value is 0 never matters. Then every combination of index values gives a different offset.
hints: Sort by coefficient, largest first. The order the digits come in doesn't matter.
For each digit, add up c · m over every digit after it. Its own coefficient must be strictly greater.
Skip digits whose largest value is 0: they're always 0, so they can't make two offsets differ or collide.
explain: This is how a mixed-radix number works: in decimal, 10 is more than 9 (the most the ones digit can add), so 23 and 14 can't collide. The sample (2, 1), (1, 2) fails: 2·1 + 1·0 and 2·0 + 1·2 are both 2, so block 1 thread 0 and block 0 thread 2 write the same element. The last big one is the GEMM's output offset per block and thread, and it passes: 8192 is more than 512·15 + 16·31 + 15 = 8191. The first big one fails: 512 is less than 32·15 + 16·31 + 15.
